the man as the only one of his kind;
comp. הַבַּעַל Baal, the lord κατ᾽ ἐξοχ.
הַשָּׂטָן Satan. Lehrg. p. 653, 654. Hence
Sept. Ἀδάμ, Vulg. Adam. b) Of a city
near the Jordan, Josh. 3, 16.
5. בֶּן־אָדָם, with art. בֶּן־הָאָדָם, son of
man, poet. for man, Num. 23, 19. Ps. 8,
very often in Ezekiel, where the prophet
is addressed from God, בֶּן־אָדָם son of
man, i. e. mortal! Ez. 2, 1. 3. 3, 1. 3. 4.
10. 4, 16. 8, 5. 6. 8. Often also in Plur.
בְּנֵי אָדָם sons of men, i. e. men, Deut.
32, 8. Ps. 11, 4. al. and with art. בְּנֵי
12. Ecc. 1, 13. Comp. Syr. ܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ son
of man, for man.
אָדֹם and אָדוֹם adj. f. אֲדֻמָּה, plur.
אֲדֻמִּים; after the form קָטֹל, קְטֻלָּה, which
is common in noting colours, see Lehrg.
§ 120. no. 21; red, ruddy, e. g. of a gar-
ment sprinkled with blood Is. 63, 2; of
ruddy cheeks Cant. 5, 10; of a chesnut
or bay-coloured horse Zech. 1, 8. 6, 2;
of a red heifer Num. 19, 2; of the red-
dish colour of lentiles Gen. 25, 30.
Subst. red, redness Is. 63, 2.
אֱדֹם pr. n. Edom. 1. The son of Isaac
and elder twin-brother of Jacob, Gen.
25, 25; more freq. called Esau, עֵשָׂו.
2. Collect. for the Edomites, the pos-
terity of Edom or Esau, and likewise for
their country, Idumea. Of the nation
Num. 20, 20; more fully בְּנֵי אֱדֹם Ps. 137,
7, and poet. בַּת אֱדֹם daughter of Edom
Lam. 4, 21. 22. Of the country, אֶרֶץ אֱדֹם
Gen. 36, 16. 21. 31; אֱדֹם Amos 1, 6; and
שְׂדֵה אֱדֹם Gen. 32, 3 [4]. Judg. 5, 4.
Where it stands alone, it is masc. when
spoken of the people, Num. 20, 20; but
fem. when it denotes the country, Jer.
49, 17. The country of the Edomites,
Idumea, was the mountainous tract be-
tween the Dead sea and the Elanitic
gulf of the Red sea, afterwards called
Gebalene, Γεβαληνή, now جبال Jebâl.
The gentile n. is אֲדֹמִי Edomite, Idu-
mean, Deut. 23, 8; plur. אֲדוֹמִים 2 K.
16, 6 Keri. Fem. אֲדֹמִית, plur. אֲדֹמִיּוֹת
Edomitish women 1 K. 11, 1.
אֹדֶם a gem of a red colour, perh. ruby,
Sept. Vulg. σάρδιον, sardius.
אֲדַמְדָּם, f. אֲדַמְדֶּמֶת, plur. f. אֲדַמְדַּמּוֹת,
adj. reddish, e. g. spots in leprous per-
sons, which are described as לְבָנוֹת
אֲדַמְדַּמּוֹת white and somewhat reddish,
אֲדָמָה f. 1. earth, Ex. 20, 24. So
called from its reddish colour; see Cred-
ner on Joel p. 125 sq.—Spec. the earth,
ground, land, as tilled, Gen. 4, 2. 47, 19.
a husbandman Gen. 9, 20; אֹהֵב אֲדָמָה a
lover of the ground, i. e. of husbandry,
2 Chr. 26, 10. Spoken of the produce
of the earth, Is. 1, 7.
2. a land, region, country, Gen. 28, 15.
אַדְמַת יְהוָֹה land of Jehovah, i. e. Canaan,
Is. 14, 2. Plur. אֲדָמוֹת lands, countries,
once Ps. 49, 12, q. d. in all lands.
3. the earth, orbis terræ, Gen. 4, 11.
4. Adamah, pr. n. of a city in Naph-
tali, Josh. 19, 36.
אַדְמָה Admah, pr. n. of a city de-
stroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah,
אַדְמוֹנִי and אַדְמֹנִי adj. (after the form
קַדְמֹנִי) red, i. e. red-haired, e. g. Esau,
42. Sept. πυῤῥάκης, Vulg. rufus.
אֲדָמִי (pr. human) Adami, pr. n. of a
city of Naphtali, Josh. 19, 33.
אֱדֹמִי see in אֱדֹם.
אַדְמָתָא Admatha, pr. n. of a Persian
nobleman, Esth. 1, 14.
* אָדַן obsol. root. 1. i. q. דּוּן, Arab.
دان mid. Waw, to be low, humble, infe-
rior. Hence אֶדֶן.
2. Transit. i. q. דִּין, to judge, to com-
mand, to domineer. Hence אָדוֹן domi-
nus, lord, and אֲדֹנָי the Lord; also
אַדָּן Addan, pr. n. of a man who re-
turned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem,
Ezra 2, 59; in the parall. passage Neh.
7, 61 written אַדּוֹן.
אֶדֶן m. plur. אֲדָנִים, constr. אַדְנֵי, a
foundation, e. g. of a column, base, pedes-
36, 38; of a building, Job 38, 6. R. אָדַן
no. 1.

line_status.note: The only difference is the mark after κατ: the print shows an elision apostrophe (κατ' for κατά before ἐξοχήν), which is properly the Greek koronis U+1FBD (᾽, Reading B), not the standalone smooth-breathing psili U+1FBF (᾿, Reading A). Hebrew הַבַּעַל (patach, dagesh in bet, patach, patach) and ἐξοχ. are printed identically in both readings and match the image.

The Syriac word is five letters ܒ‑ܪ‑ܢ‑ܫ‑ܐ (barnāšā, "son [of man]"), with pthāḥā on beth and zqāphā on nun and shin, exactly as in A; B's ܡܰܪܢܺܝܬܳܐ has the wrong initial letter, an extra yod/taw and wrong vowels, and does not match the gloss "son" that follows.
The printed word has a vav between nun and tav with the holem dot above it (plene לְבָנוֹת), not defective לְבָנֹת; Reading A drops the vav.

Both alephs carry hataf segol (three dots: sheva plus two-dot cluster visible beneath each א), not hataf patah as in Reading A — consistent with אֱדֹם "Edom". Reading B also correctly preserves the visible gap before the final period.
